solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chap, sad to say, botched raid

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning sad to say

indicators.note: a botched job is messed up, so the letters of raid are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man, regrettably, made a mess of a raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Alasdair is a Scottish male first name, so it is an example of a chap.

clue.text: Land held by rising millionaire, bilingual

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
held by says the answer is contained within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A country is owned by an up-and-coming rich person who speaks two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Land held' as the definition, but 'held by' is the hidden-word signal and 'Land' alone defines. 'rising' turns AIREBIL upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a country in West Africa, and land is a common crossword word for a nation.

clue.text: Very pleasant, with no end of sound

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: with no end says the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Something sounds very agreeable, though it never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end' cuts the last letter from NICE, leaving NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic is the adjective relating to audible waves, so it means relating to sound.

clue.text: Put on commercial broadcast in the middle

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: in the middle picks the central letter of the word broadcast

explanation.surface: An advert was screened midway through a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To add is to put on extra, as in putting on weight or a surcharge.

clue.text: Fruit shake with lemon mixed

parts.note: to rock is to shake

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of lemon are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe for a fruity drink: blend it with lemon.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockmelon is the Australian name for cantaloupe, a kind of melon.

clue.text: English poet Thomas seen in good light?

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Asks whether a famous poet appears in a flattering light.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray wrote the 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray was an eighteenth-century English writer of verse.

clue.text: Scottish city to be radiant, as golf is held in it

indicators.note: is held in it says the letters are placed inside the word for being radiant

parts.note: to glow is to be radiant
Golf is the NATO alphabet word for G

explanation.surface: A Scottish city shines because it hosts golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow is the largest urban centre in Scotland, on the Clyde.

clue.text: For each person in the lead

definitions.meaning: a head means for each person, as in ten pounds a head

explanation.surface: Each individual is out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, A HEAD is the rate per person.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ahead means being in front of rivals, and a head is a per-person rate.

clue.text: Scottish resort to herb tea infusion, last of all

indicators.note: last of all picks the final letter of each of the words in turn

explanation.surface: Someone goes to a Scottish spa to take a herbal tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a seaside town on Scotland's west coast, popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Late last month, became calmer

parts.note: December, abbreviated Dec, is the last month of the year
eased means became calmer

explanation.surface: Towards the end of last month, things settled down.
explanation.definitionFit: Late is used of someone who has died, as in the late king.

clue.text: Announce Mail Corp has been reorganised

indicators.note: reorganised says the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A news story: a newspaper company's restructuring is made public.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to declare publicly, which is to announce.

clue.text: So a drunk resolved to tour area to make enquiries

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so these letters go around the abbreviation
resolved, in the sense of broken up and reformed, says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk decided to go round the district asking questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges the first three words into ASK ROUND, and 'to tour' puts that around the abbreviation for area.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask around is the idiom for questioning various people, so to make enquiries.

clue.text: Leave Detective Sergeant in gallery

parts.note: to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A police officer is told to quit a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British theatre the gods are the highest gallery, the cheapest seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The gods is the theatre term for the topmost tier of seating.

clue.text: Frolic outside a northern Scottish town

indicators.note: outside says the word for frolic goes around the other letters

parts.note: a lark is a frolic or prank

explanation.surface: Larking about beyond a northern Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanark is a market town in South Lanarkshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Show boasted team on board plane

parts.note: to air is to show publicly
crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast

explanation.surface: A display of bragging by the flight staff.
explanation.walkthrough: CREW is the old past tense of 'crow', meaning to boast.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircrew are the pilots and attendants who work on a flight.

clue.text: Large pants legal

parts.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so awful

explanation.surface: A ruling that big underpants are permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'pants' means very bad, so it gives AWFUL, not underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawful means permitted by law, a synonym of legal.

clue.text: A French tin nearly empty? That's weird

parts.note: un is French for a
a can is a tin

indicators.note: empty says the inside of the word nearly is removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A French tin that is almost empty strikes someone as odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncanny means strange or mysterious, so it is a synonym of weird.

clue.text: Great flag to the west regularly appearing at a distance

indicators.note: to the west, in an across clue, says the letters are read right to left
regularly appearing picks every other letter from the two words

explanation.surface: A big flag can be seen far off in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly appearing' takes RAFA from GrEaT fLaG, and 'to the west' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means far away, at or from a distance.

clue.text: Cheeky old slave upset husband

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, says the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a serf was a feudal bondsman, an old kind of slave

explanation.surface: An impudent former servant annoyed a married man.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh is used of someone forward or impertinent, a sense of cheeky.

clue.text: Call with drink for bird

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
to neck is British slang for drinking quickly

explanation.surface: Phone someone and have a drink for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' is British slang for gulping a drink down.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringneck is a bird with a coloured ring around its throat, such as a parakeet.

clue.text: Specialised skill spoken of? Not at all

indicators.note: spoken of says the word is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: know-how is practical specialised skill

explanation.surface: Asked whether someone has expertise, the answer is no.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is a dialect word meaning in no way, so not at all.

clue.text: Illegal country sports event endureth sadly

indicators.note: sadly, in the sense of badly, says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A banned rural pursuit carries on, unfortunately.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunting deer with dogs was banned in England and Wales in 2004; 'country sports' is the British term for hunting and shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A deer hunt with hounds is a field sport now outlawed in Britain.

clue.text: Teeth originally without brace

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of the word teeth

parts.note: w/o is the written abbreviation for without

explanation.surface: Teeth that started out with no orthodontic brace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brace' looks like a dental device, but a brace is a pair, as of game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a pair of things, so it is the number two.

clue.text: Boy king following Dynasty

indicators.note: following says the letter for king comes after the dynasty

parts.note: the Han dynasty ruled ancient China
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A young king succeeds his royal house.
explanation.definitionFit: Hank is a male first name, short for Henry, so an example of a boy's name.

clue.text: Get warmer a week on Thursday

indicators.note: on says the following letters are placed after the day

explanation.surface: A forecast: it will be milder a week from Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: To thaw is to melt as the temperature rises above freezing.

clue.text: Do nothing right with, indeed, small openings

parts.note: taken as written
O, the figure zero, means nothing
ay is an old word for yes, indeed

explanation.surface: Instructions to do nothing properly, plus some little gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Doorways are the openings in walls where doors are hung.
